Vulnerability disclosure policy

Effective date: 15 September 2026 · VF Empire Corp Ltd, Malta, EU · Linked from security.txt (RFC 9116)

VF Empire builds software whose security claims are meant to be checked by outsiders, as the security page sets out. This policy says how to report what you find, what VF does with it, and what protection you have while you look. Report to security@vfempire.com.

1. Scope

This policy covers:

  • VF Empire products and their public repositories at github.com/vfempire-hq, including snapit-desktop, vf-privacy-kit, vfmail-desktop and vfempire-site;
  • the website vfempire.com and the services VF Empire operates for its products, such as the VF Mail node and SnapIT;
  • the privacy claims each product page makes, for example the full-offline claim on NAV·IT, which publishes a verification checklist for this purpose.

Out of scope: systems run by third parties that VF uses (GitHub, Cloudflare, the reproducibility mirrors), denial of service, social engineering of VF staff or customers, physical access, and abuse of VF services, which goes to abuse@vfempire.com. A finding outside scope is still welcome by email; section 6 and the bounty do not cover it.

2. How to report

Write to security@vfempire.com. The desk is human only: the only automated message is the acknowledgment, which arrives in under 5 seconds and includes our public key. An engineer responds within 24 hours.

Include what lets us reproduce the finding: product or repository, version or commit, steps, impact. Encrypted reports are welcome; the key is published at /.well-known/pgp.txt. If that file does not yet carry a key, send over TLS-transported email and we open an in-band shared-secret channel if the report needs one.

3. What VF does with a report

  • Response within 24 hours. We confirm receipt, assign an owner and say whether the finding is in scope.
  • Patch within a CVSS-severity-appropriate SLA. The higher the severity, the shorter the window; we give you the target date at triage.
  • Secrets are assumed compromised. A leaked credential is rotated at once, history purged with git filter-repo, and force-pushed under owner approval.
  • Public post-mortem when material. A material incident gets a public post-mortem at /post-mortems/{id} within 5 business days. A material privacy breach also triggers the refund warranty in the Terms of Service.
  • Credit. Reporters are credited unless they ask to stay anonymous.

4. Coordinated disclosure

VF works to a 90-day default disclosure window from the date of your report. We ask you to hold publication until the fix has shipped or the window has passed, whichever comes first, and we agree the date with you. If we need longer, for example because a fix touches a signed release that needs two operators in separate EU jurisdictions, we say so and explain why. The signing process is described in the signing infrastructure blueprint.

5. Bug bounty

VF pays from €500 to €25 000 per confirmed finding, tiered by severity: €500 for design-level mistakes, up to €25 000 for a novel privacy leak that breaks a claim a product page makes. Payouts are published quarterly with a severity histogram. Send bounty claims to security@vfempire.com and say so in the first line. The NAV·IT verification checklist is an explicit bounty target.

6. Safe harbour

Section 5 of the Terms of Service prohibits probing, scanning or testing the Site except under a written authorisation from VF. This policy is that authorisation for security research that is in scope (section 1), conducted in good faith and in line with sections 2, 4 and 7. For research that meets those conditions, VF Empire will not bring a legal claim against you, and will not make a complaint to a law-enforcement body about you. If a third party raises a complaint about research that complied with this policy, VF will confirm in writing that it did.

This protection is limited to VF Empire's own conduct and to systems VF controls. VF cannot authorise testing of third-party systems, and the protection ends where research goes beyond scope, retains more data than the finding needs, or harms the availability of a service.

7. What we ask of you

  • Test against your own accounts and data. If you meet another person's data, stop, record only what proves the finding, tell us, and delete it once the finding is confirmed.
  • Do not degrade a service, exhaust a resource or send bulk traffic.
  • Do not phish, impersonate or otherwise social-engineer VF staff, customers or partners.
  • Give us the disclosure window in section 4, and tell us before you publish.

8. Regulatory context

VF products ship with 24-hour vulnerability reporting under the Cyber Resilience Act; this policy is the public half of that process. Other manufacturers can adopt it through the CRA Readiness Audit and the threat model and DPIA service. Personal data in a report is handled under the Privacy Policy.

9. Questions researchers ask

How do I report a security vulnerability to VF Empire?

Email security@vfempire.com with the product or repository, the version or commit, the steps to reproduce and the impact. You get an automated acknowledgment in under 5 seconds and a response from an engineer within 24 hours. The address is read by humans only. Encrypt with the key at /.well-known/pgp.txt if you wish.

How much does the VF Empire bug bounty pay?

From €500 to €25 000 per confirmed finding, tiered by severity: €500 for design-level mistakes, up to €25 000 for a novel privacy leak that breaks a published claim. Payouts are published quarterly with a severity histogram. Claim by writing to security@vfempire.com and saying in the first line that the report is a bounty claim.

Will VF take legal action against me for security research?

No, provided the research is in scope, in good faith and in line with this policy. Section 6 is VF's written authorisation under the Terms of Service, and VF will neither bring a claim nor complain to law enforcement about compliant research. The protection covers VF's own conduct only; VF cannot authorise testing of third-party systems.

How long until a vulnerability I report is fixed?

The patch window follows CVSS severity: the higher the score, the shorter the SLA, and we give you the target date at triage. Leaked credentials are rotated at once. VF works to a 90-day default disclosure window from your report and agrees the publication date with you; a material incident gets a public post-mortem within 5 business days.

Will I be credited for the finding?

Yes, unless you ask to stay anonymous. VF credits reporters in the public post-mortem when there is one and in the quarterly bounty report. Tell us in the report how you want to be named. Anonymous reports are paid the same way; the credit line is the only thing that changes.

10. Changes and contact

VF may revise this policy; the current version is published here and referenced from security.txt. Questions: security@vfempire.com. Legal correspondence: legal@vfempire.com.
